packet.headline_seed: Australia politics live: Tim Wilson says Coalition needs time to regain trust after another poll in the doldrums
packet.description_seed: Meanwhile federal government releases options paper to improve regulation of accounting, auditing and consulting firms. Follow today’s news live Get our breaking news email , free app or daily news podcast Albanese says charges against EY employees who accessed PM’s bank account details ‘appropriate’ It’s not just KPMG in (boiling) hot water right now; EY is also in the spotlight, after two of its graduate employees on secondment at the Commonwealth Bank allegedly used the bank’s systems to access the personal details of Anthony Albanese . The two employees have been sacked. It’s before the courts and I’m not about to go into the detail of that. It’s appropriate that charges have been laid …accessing anyone’s privacy, any Australian’s privacy, is alarming, let alone someone from a contractor who’s not an employee of Commonwealth Bank being able to access that information. We’ve cracked down on that and we’ll continue to examine these issues. Quite clearly, the behaviour of some of these big accounting firms has been completely unacceptable. In some cases, it has involved breaches of the law. And they need to be held to account. Since I’ve come into this role, I’ve really tried to prioritise drawing together a lot of strands of work that were already in play. And especially now that we’ve seen what’s happened with KPMG, we’re now accelerating a lot of the government’s work. Continue reading...

what: Australia politics live: Tim Wilson says Coalition needs time to regain trust after another poll in the doldrums

clean_source_blocks.text: Meanwhile federal government releases options paper to improve regulation of accounting, auditing and consulting firms. Follow today’s news live Get our breaking news email , free app or daily news podcast Albanese says charges against EY employees who accessed PM’s bank account details ‘appropriate’ It’s not just KPMG in (boiling) hot water right now; EY is also in the spotlight, after two of its graduate employees on secondment at the Commonwealth Bank allegedly used the bank’s systems to access the personal details of Anthony Albanese . The two employees have been sacked. It’s before the courts and I’m not about to go into the detail of that. It’s appropriate that charges have been laid …accessing anyone’s privacy, any Australian’s privacy, is alarming, let alone someone from a contractor who’s not an employee of Commonwealth Bank being able to access that information. We’ve cracked down on that and we’ll continue to examine these issues. Quite clearly, the behaviour of some of these big accounting firms has been completely unacceptable. In some cases, it has involved breaches of the law. And they need to be held to account. Since I’ve come into this role, I’ve really tried to prioritise drawing together a lot of strands of work that were already in play. And especially now that we’ve seen what’s happened with KPMG, we’re now accelerating a lot of the government’s work. Continue reading...

There’s absolutely policies we need to get right, to articulate and to articulate to the Australian people. We’ve put out a series of policies already around the tax back guarantee to actually protect Australians against Jim Chalmer’s active inflation agenda. And every time we talk to people about it, they see the benefit and the advantage of it, but this is going to take time. No one’s pretending otherwise. The key thing we’ve got to do is solidify trust … and part of the challenge is we’ve got to be a sustainable alternative that clearly articulates a vision for the country. Coalition will push to ‘get the balance right’ on gambling legislation The Coalition is in the negotiation hot seat with the government to pass Labor’s gambling reforms, but they haven’t said they’ll give it the green light yet.

Peter Dutton, the former Liberal leader, had drawn up online gambling policy last term, promising to ban sports betting advertising during the broadcasting of games, one hour before and one hour after. It’s stronger than what the government’s proposed which will only cap online gambling ads to three an hour on broadcast television between 6am and 8:30pm. We know there are some in the Liberal party who want to push the government much further, including Liberal MP Simon Kennedy. Liberal frontbencher Dan Tehan, speaking to RN Breakfast this morning, says the Coalition is still in talks with the government and are keen to tighten the legislation a litle.

The Guardian Essential poll shows the Coalition is still in dire straits, with its vote being eaten up by One Nation. There’s some interesting data in the latest poll around One Nation, and a little less appetite from the public for some of their key policies – have a read below: But it also shows that while One Nation’s primary vote dropped from 28% to 26%, and Labor ticked up from 29% to 30%, the Coalition is still coming third with a very low primary vote of just 23%. So Sky News host Pete Stefanovic asks Tim Wilson why people still aren’t buying what the Liberal party is selling.

payload.title: Australian oppositio hakee luottamusta heikkojen galluplukujen keskellä
payload.summary: Australian liittopolitiikassa huomio kohdistuu sekä opposition heikkoon kannatukseen että hallituksen pyrkimyksiin kiristää suurten tilintarkastus- ja konsulttiyhtiöiden sääntelyä.
payload.content:
Australian oppositio sanoo tarvitsevansa aikaa palauttaakseen äänestäjien luottamuksen, kun tuore mielipidemittaus näyttää koalition jäävän edelleen selvästi jälkeen työväenpuolueesta ja One Nationista. Samaan aikaan liittovaltion hallitus on julkaissut vaihtoehtopaperin, jolla se hakee tiukempaa sääntelyä kirjanpito-, tilintarkastus- ja konsultointialalle useiden kohujen jälkeen.

## Koalition kannatus on paineessa

Guardian Essential -mittauksen mukaan One Nationin esivaalikannatus laski 28 prosentista 26 prosenttiin ja työväenpuolueen kannatus nousi 29 prosentista 30 prosenttiin. Koalition kannatus jäi silti kolmanneksi, 23 prosenttiin.

Liberaalipuolueen Tim Wilson sanoi, että koalition on saatava politiikkansa kohdalleen ja kerrottava se selkeämmin australialaisille. Hänen mukaansa puolue on jo esittänyt linjauksia muun muassa verotukseen liittyvästä takuusta, jolla se sanoo suojaavansa australialaisia valtiovarainministeri Jim Chalmersin inflaatiopolitiikalta.

Wilson korosti, ettei luottamuksen palautuminen tapahdu nopeasti. Hänen mukaansa koalition on rakennettava uskottava vaihtoehto ja esitettävä selkeä näkemys maan suunnasta.

## Rahapelimainonta ja konsulttiyhtiöt esillä

Koalitio neuvottelee hallituksen kanssa työväenpuolueen rahapelilainsäädännön uudistuksista, mutta ei ole vielä luvannut tukeaan esitykselle. Entinen liberaalijohtaja Peter Dutton oli aiemmin esittänyt tiukempaa linjaa, jossa urheiluvedonlyönnin mainonta kiellettäisiin ottelulähetysten aikana sekä tuntia ennen ja jälkeen niiden.

Hallituksen esitys rajoittaisi verkkorahapelimainokset kolmeen tunnissa televisiolähetyksissä kello 6:n ja 20.30:n välillä. Liberaalien riveissä osa haluaa painaa hallitusta pidemmälle, ja eturivin liberaalipoliitikko Dan Tehanin mukaan koalitio käy yhä keskusteluja ja haluaa kiristää lakia jonkin verran.

Toinen päivän keskeinen aihe on suurten asiantuntijayhtiöiden valvonta. Pääministeri Anthony Albanese piti asianmukaisena, että kahta EY:n työntekijää vastaan on nostettu syytteet tapauksessa, jossa heidän väitetään käyttäneen Commonwealth Bankin järjestelmiä pääministerin henkilökohtaisten pankkitietojen katsomiseen. Työntekijät on erotettu.

Albanesen mukaan kenen tahansa yksityisyyden loukkaaminen on vakavaa, ja erityisen huolestuttavaa on, jos tiedot ovat olleet urakoitsijan eivätkä pankin oman työntekijän käsissä. Hallitus sanoo vauhdittavansa työtä tilintarkastus-, kirjanpito- ja konsultointialan sääntelyn parantamiseksi myös KPMG:hen liittyvien tapahtumien jälkeen.

Since I’ve come into this role, I’ve really tried to prioritise drawing together a lot of strands of work that were already in play. And especially now that we’ve seen what’s happened with KPMG, we’re now accelerating a lot of the government’s work. Continue reading...

There’s absolutely policies we need to get right, to articulate and to articulate to the Australian people. We’ve put out a series of policies already around the tax back guarantee to actually protect Australians against Jim Chalmer’s active inflation agenda. And every time we talk to people about it, they see the benefit and the advantage of it, but this is going to take time. No one’s pretending otherwise. The key thing we’ve got to do is solidify trust … and part of the challenge is we’ve got to be a sustainable alternative that clearly articulates a vision for the country. Coalition will push to ‘get the balance right’ on gambling legislation The Coalition is in the negotiation hot seat with the government to pass Labor’s gambling reforms, but they haven’t said they’ll give it the green light yet.

Peter Dutton, the former Liberal leader, had drawn up online gambling policy last term, promising to ban sports betting advertising during the broadcasting of games, one hour before and one hour after. It’s stronger than what the government’s proposed which will only cap online gambling ads to three an hour on broadcast television between 6am and 8:30pm. We know there are some in the Liberal party who want to push the government much further, including Liberal MP Simon Kennedy. Liberal frontbencher Dan Tehan, speaking to RN Breakfast this morning, says the Coalition is still in talks with the government and are keen to tighten the legislation a litle.

The Guardian Essential poll shows the Coalition is still in dire straits, with its vote being eaten up by One Nation. There’s some interesting data in the latest poll around One Nation, and a little less appetite from the public for some of their key policies – have a read below: But it also shows that while One Nation’s primary vote dropped from 28% to 26%, and Labor ticked up from 29% to 30%, the Coalition is still coming third with a very low primary vote of just 23%. So Sky News host Pete Stefanovic asks Tim Wilson why people still aren’t buying what the Liberal party is selling.
